source_text: Oportuerat etiam sepultorem domini prophetari ac iam tunc merito benedici, si nec mulierum illarum officium praeterit prophetia, quae ante lucem conuenerunt ad sepulcrum cum odorum paratura. de hoc enim per Osee: et quaerent, inquit, faciem meam; ante lucem uigilabunt ad me dicentes: eamus et conuertamur ad dominum, quia ipse eripuit [dixit] et curabit nos, percussit et miserebitur nostri, sanabit nos post biduum, in die tertia resurgemus. quis enim haec non credat in recogitatu mulierum illarum uolutata inter dolorem praesentis destitutionis, qua percussae sibi uidebantur a domino, et spem resurrectionis ipsius, qua restitutuiri se arbitrabantur? corpore autem non inuento sublata erat sepultura eius de medio secundum Esaiam. sed et duo ibidem angeli apparuerunt. tot fere laterensibus uti solebat in duobus testibus consistens dei sermo. reuertentes quoque a sepulcro mulieres et ab illa angelorum uisione prospiciebatEsaias: mulieres, inquit, [uenite] uenientes a uisione, uenite, ad renuntiandam scilicet domini resurrectionem. Bene autem,I quod incredulitas discipulorum perseuerabat, ut in finem usque defensio nostra consisteret Christum legum non alium se discipulis edidisse quam prophetarum. nam cum duo ex illis iter agerent et dominus eis adhaesisset, non comparens quod ipse esset, etiam dissimulans de conscientia rei gestae: nos autem putabamus, inquiunt, ipsum esse redemptorem Israhelis, utique suum Christum, id est creatoris. adeo nec alium se ediderat illis. ceterum non existimarent eum creatoris,I et cum creatoris existimaretur, non sustinuisset hanc de se existimationem, si non is esset, qui existimabatur. aut ipse! erit auctor erroris et praeuaricator ueritatis aduersus dei optimi titulum. sed nec post resurrectionem alium se eis ostendit quam quem existimatum sibi dixerant. plane inuectus est in illos: o insensati et tardi corde in non credendo omnibus, \'quae locutus est ad uos.\' quaenam locutus? alterius se dei esse? proba, et manus dedo. an eadem et angeli ad mulieres: rememoramini, quae locutus sit uobis in Galilaea dicens, quod oportet tradi filium hominis et crucifigi et tertia die resurgere? et quare oportebat, nisi quia ita a deo creatore scriptum? igitur increpuit illos ut de sola passione scandalizatos et ut dubios de fide resurrectionis adnuntiatae sibi a feminis, per quae non crediderant ipsum fuisse, quem existimauerant. itaque quod existimauerant, id uolens credi se eum se confirmabat, quem existimauerant, creatoris scilicet Christum, redemptorem Israhelis. De corporis autem ueritate quid potest clarius? cum haesitantibus eis, ne phantasma esset, immo phantasma credentibus: quid turbati estis? (in quit,) et quid cogitationes subeunt in corda uestra? uidete manus meas et pedes, quia ipse ego sum, quoniam spiritus ossa non habet, sicut me habentem uidetis. et Marcion quaedam contraria sibi illa, credo, industria eradere de euangelio suo noluit, ut ex his, quae eradere potuit nec erasit, illa, quae erasit, aut negetur erasisse aut merito erasisse dicatur; nec parcit nisi eis, quae non minus aliter interpretando quam delendo subuertit. uult itaque sic dictum: spiritus ossa non habet, sicut me uidetis habentem, quasi ad spiritum referatur sicut me uidetis habentem, id est non habentem ossa, sicut et spiritus. et quae ratio tortuositatis istius, cum simpliciter pronuntiare potuisset:. \'quia spiritus ossa non habet, sicut me uidetis non habentem\'? cur autem inspectui eorum manus et pedes suos offert, quae membra ex ossibus constant, si ossa non habebat? cur adicit: et scitote, quia ego sum, quem scilicet corporeum retro nouerant? aut si phantasma erat usquequaque, cur illos phantasma credentes increpabat? atquin adhuc eis non credentibus propterea cibum desiderauit, ut se ostenderet etiam dentes habere. Impleuimus, ut opinor, sponsionem. exhibuimus legum Christum prophetarum doctrinis sententiis adfectibus sensibus uirtutibus passionibus etiam resun-ectione non alium quam creatoris, siquidem et apostolos mittens ad praedicandum uniuersis nationibus in omnem terram exire sonum eorum et in terminos terrae uoces eorum psalmum adimplendo praecepit. misereor tui, Marcion; frustra laborasti. Christus enim Iesus in euangelio tuo meus est.
pass_a_gloss: It was also fitting for the Lord's burial to be prophesied and already then deservedly to be blessed if not the service of those women was passed over by prophecy who before light had come together to the tomb with preparation of spices. For concerning this through Hosea he says they will seek my face and they will be vigilant to me before light saying let us go and let us turn to the Lord because he himself has taken away and he will take care of us he has struck and he will have mercy on us he will heal us after two days on the third day we will rise again. For who does not believe these things in the consideration of those women which were rolled out among the pain of the present destitution in which they seemed to themselves to have been struck by the Lord and the hope of his resurrection in which they thought they would be restored? But the burial of him was taken away from the midst according to Isaiah since the body was not found. But also two angels appeared there. Almost all the word of God consists in two witnesses as was his custom. Also Isaiah foresaw the women returning from the tomb and from that vision of the angels saying come women coming from the vision come to announce the resurrection of the Lord. It is good indeed that the incredulity of the disciples persisted so that our defense might consist to the end that Christ taught the disciples the laws not another but the prophets. For when two of them were journeying and the Lord had adhered to them not appearing because he was himself also disguising from the knowledge of the thing done we thought he was the redeemer of Israel certainly his Christ that is of the creator. So much so that he had not presented another to them. Nevertheless they did not think him to be of the creator and when he was thought to be of the creator he would not have endured this opinion about himself if he were not the one who was thought. Or would he be the author of error and the transgressor of truth against the title of the best God? But not even after the resurrection did he show himself to them other than the one they had thought. Clearly he was reproaching them o foolish and slow of heart in not believing all that he had spoken to them. What had he spoken? That he was of another God? Prove and give a hand with a finger. Or the same to the women and the angels remind yourselves what he had said to you in Galilee saying that it was necessary for the son of man to be betrayed and crucified and to rise on the third day and why was it necessary unless it was so written by God the creator? Therefore he rebuked them as having been scandalized by the passion alone and as being doubtful of the faith of the resurrection announced to them by the women through which they had not believed him to be the one they had thought. So what they had thought that is what he wanting to be believed confirmed himself to be the Christ of the creator the redeemer of Israel. But what can be clearer about the truth of the body? When they were hesitating lest it be a phantom indeed believing it to be a phantom what is disturbing you and what thoughts are entering into your hearts? See my hands and feet because I myself am he since a spirit does not have bones as you see me having. And Marcion certain things contrary to himself those I believe he did not want to erase from his gospel so that from these things which he could have erased and did not erase those things which he erased might either be denied or be said to have been erased with good reason and he does not spare except those things which having been interpreted in another way rather than being deleted subvert. He wants it to be said thus spirit does not have bones as you see me having that is not having bones as also a spirit. And what is the reason for this twisting since he could have spoken simply thus because a spirit does not have bones as you see me not having? Why does he offer his hands and feet to their sight which are members consisting of bones if he did not have bones? Why does he add and know that I am he whom you certainly knew bodily before? Or if it was a phantom why did he rebuke them believing it to be a phantom? But still not believing he desired food so that he might show himself to have teeth as well. We have fulfilled as I think the wager. We have shown the Christ of the laws the teachings the sentences the affections the senses the virtues the passions and even the resurrection not another than the creator's if indeed also sending the apostles to preach to all nations to go out into all the earth and to fulfill the psalm he commanded their sound to go out into all the earth and their voices to the ends of the earth. I pity you Marcion you have labored in vain. For Christ Jesus in your gospel is mine.

choices.why: referring to the act of burying

pass_b_english: It was also fitting that the Lord's burial be prophesied and that it already then deserved a blessing, since prophecy did not overlook the service of those women who gathered at the tomb before dawn with spices prepared. For Hosea speaks of this: they will seek my face; before dawn they will keep vigil toward me, saying, 'Let us go and turn back to the Lord, for he has torn and will heal us; he has struck and will have mercy on us; he will heal us after two days, and on the third day we will rise again' (Hosea). Who could refuse to believe this when considering those women, tossed between the pain of their present destitution, in which they seemed struck by the Lord, and the hope of his resurrection, by which they expected to be restored? But once his body was not found, his burial was removed from the midst, according to Isaiah (Isaiah). And two angels appeared there as well. Almost all of God's word, as was his custom, stands on two witnesses. Isaiah also foresaw the women returning from the tomb and from that vision of the angels: 'Come, women coming from the vision; come to announce the Lord's resurrection' (Isaiah).

It is a good thing, indeed, that the disciples' incredulity persisted to the very end, so that our defense would stand firm: Christ taught the disciples the Law, but he presented himself to them as no other than the prophets. For when two of them were traveling and the Lord joined them, not appearing as he truly was, but even disguising himself from their knowledge of what had happened, they said, 'We thought he was the redeemer of Israel, certainly his Christ -- that is, the Creator's.' So completely had he not presented another to them. Yet they did not think him to be of the Creator; and when he was thought to be the Creator's, he would not have endured that opinion about himself if he were not the one they thought he was. Otherwise, he would be the author of error and a falsifier of the truth against the title of the best God. But not even after the resurrection did he show himself to them as anyone other than the one they had thought him to be. Clearly he reproached them: 'O foolish ones, and slow of heart to believe all that he spoke to you' (Luke 24:25). What had he spoken? That he was of another God? Prove it, and I will concede the point. Or did the angels say the same to the women: 'Remember what he told you in Galilee, that the Son of Man must be delivered and crucified and rise on the third day' (Luke 24:6-7)? And why was it necessary, unless it was so written by God the Creator? Therefore he rebuked them as those scandalized by the passion alone and doubtful of the resurrection faith announced to them by women, through whom they had not believed him to be the one they had thought. So, what they had thought -- that is what he, wanting to be believed, confirmed himself to be: the Christ of the Creator, the Redeemer of Israel.

What could be clearer about the truth of the body? When they were hesitating, lest it be a phantom -- indeed, believing it to be a phantom -- he said, 'Why are you troubled, and why do doubts arise in your hearts? See my hands and my feet, that I myself am he; for a spirit does not have bones, as you see me having' (Luke 24:38-39). And Marcion, I believe, did not want to erase certain things contrary to himself from his gospel, so that from those he could erase but did not, those he did erase might either be denied or said to have been rightly erased; and he spares only those things which, by interpreting them differently rather than deleting them, he subverts. He wants the text to read: 'A spirit does not have bones, as you see me having' -- that is, not having bones, just as a spirit does not. What is the reason for this twisting, since he could have spoken simply: 'Because a spirit does not have bones, as you see me not having'? Why does he offer his hands and feet for inspection, limbs consisting of bones, if he had no bones? Why does he add, 'Know that I am he' -- whom, namely, they had known bodily before? Or if he was a phantom through and through, why did he rebuke them for believing it to be a phantom? Yet while they still did not believe, he asked for food, to show that he even had teeth. We have fulfilled, I think, the wager. We have shown the Christ of the Law -- in teachings, judgments, affections, senses, virtues, passions, and even resurrection -- to be none other than the Creator's. For by sending the apostles to preach to all nations, to go out into all the earth, he commanded their sound to go out into all the earth and their words to the ends of the world, fulfilling the Psalm (Psalm 19:4). I pity you, Marcion; you have labored in vain. For Christ Jesus in your gospel is mine.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Scripture citations in Pass B (Hosea, Isaiah, Luke 24:25, Luke 24:6-7, Luke 24:38-39, and Psalm 19:4) correctly identify the biblical loci alluded to or quoted in the Latin. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source and each other.
